The study compares ring, crosses, and Y-aperture FSS units with the same center frequency of 13.5 GHz.
Double-layer radar absorbing materials have a resonance frequency of 4.1 GHz with -12.3 dB reflectivity and 1.5 GHz bandwidth at -6 dB.
The ring unit FSS has a radius of 3.34 mm and slit width of 0.6 mm.
The crosses unit FSS has arm length 4.1 mm and arm width 0.62 mm.
The Y-aperture unit FSS has arm length 4.8 mm and slit width 0.5 mm.
All FSS units cause the resonance frequency of the absorbing materials to shift to higher frequencies.
The crosses unit causes the largest resonance frequency shift to 5.6 GHz.
The ring unit causes a smaller resonance frequency shift to 5.2 GHz.
The Y-aperture unit shifts resonance frequency to 5.4 GHz.
The ring unit decreases resonance frequency reflectivity by 2.2 dB to -14.5 dB.
The crosses unit reflectivity at resonance frequency is -12.6 dB.
The Y-aperture unit increases resonance frequency reflectivity by 1.3 dB to -11 dB.
The Y-aperture unit expands the -6 dB bandwidth from 1.5 GHz to 4.8 GHz.
The crosses unit expands the bandwidth to 4.4 GHz, and the ring unit to 2.3 GHz.
The substrate for FSS units is a cellular board with 3 mm thickness and dielectric constant 1.007.
Spectral domain method combined with moment method and rooftop basis functions was used for electromagnetic simulation.
The study provides design guidance: Y-aperture units are ideal for bandwidth expansion, ring units for reducing resonance frequency drift and reflectivity.

The double-layer absorbing material parameters are: first layer thickness 0.5 mm, dielectric constant 5.91-j2.41, permeability 1.04-j0.04; second layer thickness 1.5 mm, dielectric constant 20.60-j3.07, permeability 1.13-j0.87.
The FSS units are arranged in square arrays with a period of 10 mm.
The incident wave polarization in simulations is TE with 0° incident angle.
